newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia hunts fugitive Philippines legislator.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia hunts fugitive Philippines legislator.

text.p: Indonesian police are hunting fugitive Philippine legislator Romeo Jalosjos, wanted on charges of statutory rape of an 11-year old girl, the official Antara news agency reported.
"We hope we could immediately find the Philippine legislator," Brigadier-General Ahwil Lutan, head of the Indonesian Interpol Secretariat, told Antara.

Foreign Affairs Secretary Domingo Siazon said in Manila on Friday the Philippines had asked Indonesia to help find Jalosjos. He said Manila has cancelled Jalosjos's diplomatic passport early this week.

Members of the ethics committee of the House of Representatives unanimously voted on Thursday to recommend the suspension of Jalosjos for 60 days after a 72-hour deadline set by the legislature for him to surrender to the police expired.

Jalosjos, a member of President Fidel Ramos's ruling coalition in the legislature, has evaded arrest since a Manila judge on December 26 issued 14 separate warrants of arrest against him for two counts of statutory rape and 12 acts of lasciviousness.
President Fidel Ramos last week ordered a hunt for Jalosjos during mounting media criticism of police failure to locate the lawmaker.

General Manuel Pepino, head of a police task force in the southern Mindanao region, said on Thursday he had information that Jalosjos left the country on a speedboat from a southern beach resort on December 26 for Indonesia.

State prosecutors filed statutory rape charges against Jalosjos after an 11-year-old girl gave a statement saying the legislator had sexual relations with her several times in his Manila apartment last year, paying her amounts ranging up to 10,000 pesos ($385) each time.

The prosecutors said the girl's father brought her to the politician in exchange for money. The father faces a separate charge of exploitation. Jalosjos was earlier reported by some newspapers to have gone to Malaysia.
